lead.headline: Iran says it struck at U.S. radar in Bahrain as third U.S. carrier reaches region
more: The Guards had claimed on Friday that they destroyed a U.S. early-warning radar in Bahrain in retaliation for a strike on a telecommunications tower in Sirik, on Iran's Hormuz coast. U.S. Central Command denied that, saying U.S. forces shot down two drones and there was no damage. The U.S. military had not commented on Sunday's claim.

The Roosevelt joins the carriers George H.W. Bush and George Washington and the amphibious ship Boxer group, Axios reported, citing a U.S. official. Iran says the Strait of Hormuz remains closed, and Washington has kept up its naval blockade and tightened sanctions while Tehran sets conditions for any deal.
lead.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they launched six drones at a U.S. air defense radar at Riffa Air Base in Bahrain on Sunday, citing what they called hostile U.S. actions, according to the IRGC-affiliated Fars news agency. Bahrain's military said its air defenses thwarted several Iranian aerial attacks, and residents were sent to shelters twice in about three hours; no casualties were reported. The same day a U.S. official said the aircraft carrier USS Theodore Roosevelt had arrived in the Middle East, the third carrier in the region. Talks to end the war, now more than eight months old, remain stalled.

briefs.text: Former Credit Suisse chairman Urs Rohner personally ordered the bank's surveillance of Greenpeace after activists disrupted its 2017 shareholder meeting in Zurich, the SonntagsZeitung reported. The bank's spying on the group became public in 2020.

The city of Zurich's minimum wage of 23.90 francs an hour will take effect on January 1, 2027, after the Federal Court upheld it in May; employers have until the end of 2027 to comply. Voters approved it in 2023 with about 70 percent support.
Investors in US ski operator Vail Resorts are questioning its Swiss investments in Andermatt and Crans-Montana, the NZZ am Sonntag reported. Vail said it believes it can grow there.

stories.headline: Thousands march in Geneva against cantonal spending cuts
more: The draft budget includes savings of 247.7 million francs, among them across-the-board 4 percent subsidy cuts for associations and 5 percent reductions in service contracts with the Geneva University Hospitals and a home-care provider. The march was organized by a coalition of trade unions, associations and left-wing parties and ended with a performance by an orchestra of about 50 musicians.
The cantonal parliament is due to debate the budget in mid-December. Similar rallies have taken place in Lausanne, and another is planned in Neuchatel on November 20.
stories.summary: Thousands of people marched through Geneva on Saturday to protest austerity measures in the canton's draft 2027 budget. Police put turnout at about 3,500, organizers at 6,000 to 7,000, and a Keystone-SDA count at just under 5,000; no incidents were reported.

stories.headline: Report says Swiss-made ammunition reached Russia after 2022 invasion
more: The manufacturer, now called SwissP Defence and owned by Italy's Beretta Holding since 2022, said it supplies customers only within the law. The State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO) is examining the report.

Separately, the SonntagsZeitung reported that Brazilian police seized about 1,500 Swiss-made rifle cartridges in 2018 and 2019, in one case destined for a drug cartel. SwissP Defence said it has never exported ammunition to an embargoed country.
stories.summary: The NZZ am Sonntag reported, citing Russian Economy Ministry data, that two companies registered deliveries of 110,000 rounds of high-precision ammunition from the former Ruag Ammotec after February 2022. The suspected route ran through the Balkans to Central Asia; the original Swiss export to Slovenia was legal.

briefs.text: Austrian President Alexander Van der Bellen spoke at the central Remembrance Sunday ceremony in the Bundestag on Sunday, attended by President Frank-Walter Steinmeier and Defense Minister Boris Pistorius.

The governing coalition's leaders meet on Tuesday and may discuss cutting the electricity tax for all consumers, at a cost of about 5.4 billion euros not included in the 2027 budget; Klingbeil said he is open to it if it can be financed.
Three people were killed when a car plunged off a bridge in Baden-Baden on Sunday.
The German Weather Service forecast a gray, wet and windy week starting Monday.

stories.headline: Hubertus Heil launches bid for SPD leadership, challenging Klingbeil
more: Klingbeil, who has led the party alone since Barbel Bas stepped down in October, told about 120 Brandenburg party members in Potsdam on Sunday that the party must act in unison and again defended combining the party leadership with a cabinet post. He said the party presidium would make a personnel proposal by December 16 at the latest.
Several SPD working groups and the Jusos youth wing have filed motions to bar the party chair from holding a federal ministry. The leadership will be elected at a party congress in Bremen in January.
stories.summary: Former labor minister Hubertus Heil has become the first candidate to announce a run for chair of the Social Democrats, in a move seen as a challenge to Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil. The Saxony-Anhalt SPD nominated Heil, and its chair Andreas Schmidt said he connects eastern and western Germany like few others.

stories.headline: Left Party pressure grows on Berlin lawmaker as coalition talks continue
more: Ramelow told ZDF that Emde signed the joint exploratory paper with the SPD and Greens and publicly took the opposite position the next day, but said she could keep her directly won seat. The Berlin Left wants to expel her from the group, with a decision expected this week, ZDF reported.
stories.summary: Senior Left Party politician Bodo Ramelow urged Berlin state lawmaker Vanessa Emde to leave her party's parliamentary group, accusing her of a breach of trust. The Left, the SPD and the Greens are negotiating a coalition in Berlin, and the SPD national leadership has demanded the Left act against members accused of antisemitism.

stories.headline: VW chief targets record 9 percent margin by 2030
more: Blume said the cuts were not a radical blow and noted the company is spending billions, including on severance agreements.
stories.summary: Volkswagen CEO Oliver Blume said the group aims for a 9 percent return by 2030, a level it has never reached, with sales of about 9 million vehicles worldwide. In an interview, he defended cutting more than 100,000 jobs, citing German labor costs roughly twice those elsewhere in Europe.

briefs.text: Canada pledged up to $560 million over four years to the Tropical Forest Forever Facility, a Brazil- and Norway-led fund that pays tropical countries for verified forest protection and directs at least 20% of payments to Indigenous Peoples and local communities, Prime Minister Mark Carney's office said.

Cacao planting in Brazil's Pará state grew about a third from 2022 to 2024, to 116,436 hectares, and 96% of it sits on land cleared before 2020 rather than newly cut forest, according to mapping by the state agricultural research agency Embrapa.

stories.headline: Antarctic blue whales are slowly coming back
more: The University of Washington-led team, working with NOAA, the Australian Marine Mammal Centre and others, combined historical catch records, ship surveys and photo identification of individual whales to model the population.

The whales remain listed as critically endangered and breed slowly, with one calf every two to three years. The authors say whether they can return to pre-whaling numbers is an open question and call for continued monitoring in international waters.
stories.summary: Antarctic blue whales, hunted to about 418 animals by the early 1970s, now number an estimated 4,018 and are growing about 4.5% a year, according to a study published Nov. 5 in Endangered Species Research. The population is still only about 1.9% of its size before commercial whaling, which once counted hundreds of thousands of the animals.

briefs.text: Sweden Democrat MP Rasmus Giertz is resigning from parliament after several young women accused him of sexual misconduct in a Dagens Nyheter investigation; he rejects the allegations but said stepping down was best for the party.
Heavy snow hit northern Sweden late last week, stranding 60 to 100 vehicles overnight on the E4 near Ornskoldsvik, while icy roads were reported in the south.

stories.headline: Centre Party picks Social Democrats for government talks
more: Andersson wants a government of the Social Democrats, the Centre Party and the Greens, which would also need the Left Party's backing in parliament. She called the decision very welcome and said she would start the next phase of talks with the Left, Centre and Green parties; the Greens also welcomed it.

Thand Ringqvist said policy content, financing of major reforms and parliamentary support remain open. Sweden has been without a new government since the September election, which gave the centre-left a slim majority.
stories.summary: Sweden's Centre Party said late Sunday it will continue negotiations on the basis of Social Democrat leader Magdalena Andersson's proposal rather than that of Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson's Moderates. Leader Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist made support conditional on the Left Party dropping its demand for cabinet posts.

briefs.text: A Copa Airlines Boeing 737 with 172 people aboard and a UPS cargo jet collided on a taxiway at Miami International Airport on Saturday night; two people had minor injuries, and the NTSB is investigating.

A federal judge blocked the administration until Nov. 28 from closing East Potomac Park and its public golf course in Washington, calling the government's reasons pretextual; Trump said the administration will appeal.

stories.headline: Trump-picked RNC chair faces challenge after midterm losses
more: Critics want a forensic audit of party spending, including hair and makeup services for Trump and other officials, a $22,500 hospitality bill at a golf event and a brief contract with a daughter of former White House chief of staff Susie Wiles. Gruters has defended the spending.

Crosbie's support is thought to be small, though one backer said she expects the 20 votes needed. Trump has publicly backed Gruters. Members vote at the winter meeting in Arizona in January, and the outcome will shape the party's role in the 2028 nominating contest.
stories.summary: A group of Republican National Committee members is backing a challenge to chairman Joe Gruters, whom President Trump handpicked, after the party's worst midterm showing in a generation. KC Crosbie, the committee's co-chair from Kentucky, announced her bid in a letter to members.

stories.headline: Tanker's steering failed before it hit a river cruise ship, NTSB says
more: The cruise ship, carrying 140 passengers and 50 crew, later capsized, and people including two police officers were thrown into the river. Thirty-two people went to hospitals; none were critically hurt, and six remained hospitalized Sunday.
The NTSB expects a preliminary report within 30 days. The Port of New Orleans has sued the tanker's owners for at least $1 million in terminal damage.
stories.summary: The National Transportation Safety Board said Sunday that a preliminary finding shows the steering on the tanker Atlantic Asphalt failed, leaving its rudder turned to the right, before it struck the cruise ship American Heritage on the Mississippi River on Friday. The cause of the failure is not yet known.

stories.headline: SpaceX catches a Starship returning from orbit for the first time
more: Reusing the ship is central to SpaceX's plan to cut launch costs. The company still has to show it can recover vehicles reliably and refuel them in orbit, with fueling tests planned over the next several flights, before Starship can serve as a lunar lander for NASA.
stories.summary: SpaceX caught its Starship upper stage with the mechanical arms of its launch tower at Starbase, Texas, on Saturday after about 22 hours in space, the first recovery of the vehicle from orbit. The Super Heavy booster was lost after a guidance problem diverted it offshore, where it ran out of fuel and exploded just before reaching the water.

Zelenskyy said restrictions on Ukraine's use of the Starshield satellite system, which he said appear to come from SpaceX, keep interceptor drones from catching Russian Shahed drones and threaten energy defenses before winter.
Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi fired nine senior security and oil officials over an alleged oil smuggling ring in Jurf al-Nasr, a stronghold of the Iran-backed Kataib Hezbollah.
Hungarian investigators found about $19.5 million in cash hidden in forests, farm buildings and a home in a bribery probe into former development minister Miklos Sesztak, who denies wrongdoing.

stories.headline: Zelenskyy says U.S. asked about leaving Donbas in exchange for NATO membership
more: Zelenskyy said Ukraine would need guarantees modeled on NATO's mutual defense clause plus troops, weapons and money, and that he was not sure the idea would work. He said he could not decide alone and would put any territorial exchange to Ukrainians if NATO and EU guarantees were offered.

Russian President Vladimir Putin has demanded that Ukraine pull out of Donbas before any peace deal. U.S. envoy Jared Kushner said separately that he hopes to broker talks between Europe and Russia on the war.
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said U.S. negotiators asked whether Ukraine would withdraw from the Donbas region if it were allowed to join NATO, the first time the idea had been raised with him. There was no U.S. confirmation of his account.

stories.headline: Congo's Ebola outbreak still out of control six months on
more: The Africa CDC says 80 percent of new cases are found outside the surveillance system, and about a third of deaths happen at home or in the community. Strikes by unpaid health workers, attacks on clinics and armed conflict are hampering the response, and more than $700 million in aid is unaccounted for.
UNICEF says children made up 35 percent of deaths through Nov. 4. Experts see little chance of bringing the outbreak under control within a year.
stories.summary: Six months after Congo declared the outbreak, government figures show more than 11,000 Ebola cases, with nearly half of those infected dying, making it the deadliest of the country's 17 outbreaks. The virus has reached eight of Congo's 26 provinces, and Nigeria, Kenya and Uganda have confirmed cases.

stories.headline: Southeast Asian leaders open summit in Manila ahead of Trump's arrival
more: Trump is set to join a Quad meeting with Japan, Australia and India and a special U.S.-ASEAN summit on Tuesday, meet Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. on Wednesday and then fly to Shenzhen for the APEC summit. Chinese Premier Li Qiang meets ASEAN leaders Monday and leaves before Trump arrives.
stories.summary: Leaders of the 11-nation Association of Southeast Asian Nations opened a three-day summit in Manila on Sunday, with the Middle East war, South China Sea disputes and Myanmar's civil war at the top of the agenda. President Trump is due to arrive Tuesday with Secretary of State Marco Rubio.

asl.hook: The two index fingers are two people meeting.
steps: NICE: hold your non-dominant hand in front of you, palm up.
Slide the flat palm of your dominant hand across it once; Lifeprint notes this is also the sign for CLEAN.
MEET: make an index-finger handshape with each hand, holding the non-dominant hand out away from your body.
Move the dominant index finger from you toward the other hand so the two meet in the middle, without the fingertips touching.
asl.tip: Use index fingers, not a D handshape: Lifeprint warns that D turns it into Nice to date you.

lead.headline: Trump, Xi and Putin to hold first three-way summit in China next week
more: The New START treaty expired in February, leaving the U.S. and Russia without limits on nuclear arsenals for the first time in more than 50 years.

Trump travels first to the Philippines for an ASEAN summit and will also hold a working lunch and meeting with Xi on Thursday, their fourth since he returned to office. Elon Musk will travel with him but will not join the three-way meeting.
lead.summary: The White House said President Trump is expected to meet Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin on Thursday on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen, the first formal meeting of its kind among the three. Trump plans to raise cutting nuclear arsenals and the Iran war, while U.S. officials said Russia's war in Ukraine and chip export controls are not on the agenda. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov called the meeting extremely significant. A senior administration official said no agreement is expected.

briefs.text: Swiss International Air Lines said Saturday it still expected some delays after a four-hour halt on departures from US airports, but that operations should steadily return to normal.
German conductor Mats Thiersch won the conducting prize at the 80th Concours de Geneve, leading the Orchestre de la Suisse Romande at Victoria Hall; the first prize is worth 20,000 francs.

stories.headline: Hundreds of men rally in Bern against violence toward women
more: The rally was co-organized by social worker Christoph Gosteli and the men's group maenner. A June study by the University of Zurich and the umbrella group MenCare found that half of male respondents aged 18 to 24 held a dominance-based view of masculinity, and called for a broad debate starting in schools.
Justice Minister Beat Jans said in a speech earlier this month that men commit four-fifths of violent crimes and account for up to 99 percent of rape cases.
stories.summary: Hundreds of men gathered on the Bundesplatz outside the federal parliament in Bern on Saturday to denounce misogyny and violence against women. Organizers said men must take a bigger role in tackling the problem, pointing to concern about misogynistic content spreading online among teenage boys and young men.

stories.headline: Cassis represents Switzerland at Francophonie summit in Cambodia
more: The summit will choose a secretary-general for the next four years from four candidates, including outgoing chief Louise Mushikiwabo of Rwanda and former Romanian prime minister Dacian Ciolos.
The organization has 90 member states and governments, including observers. It is only the second Francophonie summit held in Asia, after Hanoi in 1997.
stories.summary: Foreign Minister Ignazio Cassis is in Phnom Penh for the 20th summit of the Francophonie, which runs Sunday and Monday. Switzerland plans to promote its mediation and good-offices work and the role of International Geneva in digital governance, and to sign a new peacebuilding partnership with the organization.

briefs.text: Hundreds of mourners attended a state memorial in Munich for Bavarian Deputy Premier and Free Voters leader Hubert Aiwanger, who was found dead in a Berlin hotel room this month aged 55; an autopsy found natural causes.
The far-right AfD plans to nominate former World Cup winner Thomas Berthold as its candidate in the January 30, 2027, election for federal president.
Deductions for taking a pension early are set to rise from 0.3 to 0.4 percent per month, CSU parliamentary leader Alexander Hoffmann said.
The German Weather Service warned of black ice overnight into Sunday, especially in Rhineland-Palatinate and Saarland.
A cup of mulled wine is expected to cost about 5 euros at large Christmas markets this year, up from an average of 4.54 euros last year.

stories.headline: Klingbeil's future as SPD leader in question ahead of January congress
more: The SPD will elect a new two-person leadership at a party congress in Bremen in mid-January 2027. Klingbeil has not said whether he will run and is touring the party to test his support, saying he is not clinging to his seat.

Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania premier Manuela Schwesig is the name most often mentioned as an alternative but has not decided. Defense Minister Boris Pistorius has ruled himself out and backed Klingbeil.
stories.summary: Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil defended holding both his cabinet post and the Social Democratic Party leadership after a Spiegel report that party working groups want to stop him from running again. He has led the SPD alone since co-leader Barbel Bas resigned in October.

stories.headline: Merz to host Coalition of the Willing in Berlin on Thursday
more: The meeting, titled United for Peace in Ukraine and European Security, will also discuss further support for Ukraine, the government said. It follows an EU decision this week that Germany, France, Britain, Italy and Poland will join the bloc at the next round of peace talks.
stories.summary: Chancellor Friedrich Merz, French President Emmanuel Macron and British Prime Minister Andy Burnham have invited the so-called Coalition of the Willing to meet at the Chancellery in Berlin on November 19. The talks are meant to coordinate diplomacy and set out security guarantees for Ukraine after the war.

briefs.text: China connected a 60-megawatt liquid-air energy storage plant in Golmud, Qinghai, to the grid on Oct. 30; it stores 600 megawatt-hours, enough for 10 hours of output, and its developer calls it the world's largest of its kind.

A survey of the remote Bikar and Bokak atolls in the Marshall Islands, now a marine sanctuary of about 48,000 square kilometers, recorded at least 266 groups of reef fish, 132 green turtle nest pits and two groups possibly new to science, according to a study published Nov. 11.

U.S. homelessness fell an estimated 6.7% in 2026 to about 693,000 people, roughly 49,000 fewer than a year earlier and the largest one-year drop since 2007, according to an analysis for the National Alliance to End Homelessness.

stories.headline: Two Bundibugyo Ebola vaccines cleared for trials in Congo
more: The recommendation, published Nov. 4, followed reviews of animal studies and interim phase 1 safety and immune-response data. Both vaccines are to join the Tumaini trial, which began Oct. 23 in Bunia and vaccinates contacts of people who fell ill, an approach known as ring vaccination.
Trials could start within three to four weeks once Congolese regulators approve them, and first results could come in early 2027, according to Health Policy Watch.
stories.summary: A World Health Organization advisory group unanimously recommended that two experimental vaccines against Bundibugyo virus, a strain of Ebola with no approved vaccine or treatment, be tested in a phase 2/3 trial in the Democratic Republic of Congo. The candidates are ChAdOx1 BDBV from the University of Oxford and the Serum Institute of India, and Moderna's mRNA-1469.

briefs.text: Centre Party leader Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist is using the weekend to weigh rival government offers from Social Democrat Magdalena Andersson and caretaker Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson; Sweden faces a new election within three months if the deadlock continues.

The Riksdag approved a constitutional change 292 to 51 that allows future laws to revoke the citizenship of dual nationals who obtained it on false grounds or are convicted of crimes seriously harming Sweden's vital interests; the next government must still bring a bill.
Sweden beat Bosnia and Herzegovina 3-2 in the Nations League in Solna, with two Viktor Gyokeres penalties, to stay top of Group B4 with one match left, at Poland on Tuesday.

stories.headline: Sweden moves to bar Russian athletes ahead of Falun ski championships
more: Finland and Norway announced similar steps on Thursday. The International Ski and Snowboard Federation allows Russian and Belarusian athletes to compete under conditions such as no national symbols; the Swedish Ski Association disagrees but says it will comply.

In October, the Court of Arbitration for Sport cleared the way for Russian ice hockey teams to return to world championships next year, and Sweden urged the EU to tighten visa rules for Russian and Belarusian athletes.
stories.summary: Sweden is preparing measures to deny entry to Russian athletes, Social Affairs Minister Jakob Forssmed told AFP, with the aim of having them in place before the Nordic World Ski Championships in Falun begin in February. He said Russian sport is closely tied to the state and that its participation could serve as propaganda and normalize the war in Ukraine.

briefs.text: Police in Peoria, Illinois, rendered safe a suspicious package found near the BioUrja ethanol plant on Friday after evacuating everyone within a mile; searches for other possible devices continued and no arrests were reported.

The Brooklyn district attorney opened a criminal investigation into Wednesday's collapse of a Brooklyn apartment building into a neighboring construction site, which killed eight people, including two children.
Family Dollar agreed to pay $63 million to settle claims by the FTC and 17 states that it charged shoppers more than shelf and advertised prices, including a $40 million fund for customers.
Dr. Brian Monahan, the attending physician of the U.S. Capitol and a Navy rear admiral, resigned amid misconduct allegations, Senate Majority Leader John Thune said.

stories.headline: U.S. loses measles elimination status for the first time since 2000
more: The CDC has counted 5,412 cases in 2026, more than double last year's total, in 45 states and Washington, D.C. More than 590 people have been hospitalized, and about 96 percent of cases were in people who were unvaccinated or whose status was unknown. Pennsylvania has the largest outbreak, with more than 1,500 cases.

PAHO is due to hold a news conference on Tuesday. Regaining the status would require ending local spread, which PAHO says takes at least 95 percent vaccination coverage along with strong surveillance and fast outbreak response.
stories.summary: The Pan American Health Organization has decided the United States no longer meets the standard for measles elimination, researchers familiar with the decision told KFF Health News on Saturday. A country keeps the status only if no outbreak spreads locally for 12 months or longer, and about a third of this year's cases trace to outbreaks that began in 2025.

stories.headline: Old routers blamed for nationwide ground stop as cancellations run into Saturday
more: Friday's stop began at 3:36 p.m. EST with about 3,500 planes in the air and was lifted around 8:20 p.m. All airborne flights landed safely. FlightAware counted about 9,159 cancellations on Friday. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said there were no signs of a cyberattack.

Duffy said restoring capacity would take time but that he expects normal operations by the Thanksgiving travel rush, which begins in under two weeks. The disruption also scrambled travel plans for NBA, NHL and college football teams.
stories.summary: A preliminary FAA review traced Friday's nationwide ground stop to a telecommunications failure. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said FAA routers became overloaded with data, and senior government sources told CBS News the problem was confined to Cisco routers made between 2001 and 2006. More than 3,800 flights were canceled on Saturday, according to FlightAware.

stories.headline: Justices agree to hear challenge to Trump's border asylum ban
more: Trump issued the proclamation on his first day back in office, citing an "invasion" at the border, and immigration authorities have used it to remove migrants without letting them apply for asylum. The appeals court paused its ruling pending Supreme Court review, so the policy remains in force. A decision is expected by the end of June or early July.
stories.summary: The Supreme Court agreed to review President Trump's proclamation suspending access to asylum for migrants who cross the southern border between ports of entry. A federal judge in Washington ruled the policy unlawful, and a divided appeals court panel agreed in April that it exceeded the president's authority.

briefs.text: A court in Makati ordered the arrest of jailed Philippine preacher Apollo Quiboloy and two officers of his sect, a step toward possible extradition to the United States, where he faces child sex trafficking charges.

stories.headline: Iran says mines hit tankers in Hormuz as Trump says no deal is needed
more: President Trump said on Thursday the U.S. no longer needs a deal with Tehran and told Vice President JD Vance to focus on domestic issues, while warning U.S. forces were ready to act. Iran's deputy UN ambassador told the Security Council that Iran has never closed the door to diplomacy. Diplomats describe peace efforts as stalled, with Qatar seeking an interim deal on Hormuz traffic.

The International Energy Agency said global oil supply has overtaken demand for the first time since the war began. Brent crude was near $96 a barrel on Friday, against about $72 before the war, CBS News reported.
stories.summary: Iran's navy said a tanker struck a naval mine and caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz, the fourth such incident in 24 hours, and accused the vessel of entering prohibited waters. The United States says it has cleared the main shipping routes of mines. The UN called for an end to deadly attacks on shipping.

stories.headline: Zelenskyy warns U.S.-floated European security framework could help Putin
more: Zelenskyy said a planned prisoner exchange would involve roughly 1,200 to 1,300 people on each side. Ukraine said it hit an oil pipeline station in Russia's Samara region and the Lipetsk-2 airfield; Moscow did not comment. A Russian attack on Zaporizhzhia injured 22 people, including three children, the AP reported.
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy called a new European security framework raised by Washington dangerous, saying Moscow could use it to weaken NATO and redraw borders. He said the U.S. had asked whether Kyiv would leave parts of Donbas that Russia does not control in exchange for NATO membership, and repeated that Ukraine will not give up territory.

stories.headline: ICC judges halt probe into alleged U.S. crimes in Afghanistan
more: The U.S. part of the inquiry had been dormant since 2021. Washington, which does not recognize the court, has sanctioned 13 current and former ICC staff, and Secretary of State Marco Rubio said President Trump will never allow the court to prosecute Americans.
stories.summary: Judges at the International Criminal Court stopped the prosecutor's investigation into alleged crimes by American troops in Afghanistan, citing major limits on gathering evidence, and redirected the case toward the Taliban's conduct since 2021. The ruling also closed the probe into the Islamic State affiliate ISKP, and the prosecutor's office has appealed.

asl.hook: Your fist is a little head nodding yes.
steps: Make an S handshape: a closed fist.
Hold the fist up in front of you; it stands for your head.
Bend at the wrist to raise and lower the fist, like a head nodding yes.
Nod your head along with it; Lifeprint notes ASL affirms with a head nod.
asl.tip: NO is the other half of this pair: Lifeprint lists a firm single motion as a command and a double motion with a small headshake as the standard form.

onThisDay.text: Apollo 12 lifted off from Kennedy Space Center with Pete Conrad, Dick Gordon and Alan Bean on NASA's second crewed Moon landing mission. The Saturn V was struck by lightning twice in the first minute of flight but flew on undamaged. Five days later, Conrad and Bean landed in the Ocean of Storms, just 535 feet from the Surveyor 3 probe.

lead.headline: FAA halts all U.S. departures for four hours after air traffic communications failure
more: More than 3,500 aircraft were in the air when the stop was issued, and at least 827 flights had been diverted by early evening, according to Cirium data cited by the Associated Press. FlightAware counted about 7,000 delayed or canceled flights, Al Jazeera reported.

Officials linked the outage to overloaded switches and routers in the FAA's aging telecommunications network; newer digital equipment kept working while older analog systems failed. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said communications had been restored and the exact cause remains under investigation.

It was the first nationwide ground stop since a January 2023 FAA computer failure. The FAA and the White House asked Congress on Friday for another $30.1 billion to modernize the air traffic control system, on top of $12.5 billion approved last year.
lead.summary: The Federal Aviation Administration ordered a rare nationwide ground stop on Friday afternoon after a communications problem hit the air route traffic control centers that guide high-altitude traffic. The stop began at about 3:54 p.m. ET and was lifted at 8:15 p.m. ET, AVweb reported. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said investigators found no evidence of a cyberattack. Airlines warned that delays and cancellations would continue as planes and crews are moved back into position.

briefs.text: Switzerland will host the next European Political Community summit in Zurich on April 15, 2027, the government said after President Parmelin attended this week's summit in Dublin.
Swiss unemployment by the international ILO measure rose to 5.6 percent in the third quarter, up from 5.1 percent a year earlier, while the number of people in work grew 0.5 percent.
Swiss producer and import prices rose 0.9 percent in October from September, led by petroleum products, the Federal Statistical Office said.
The average car collision claim cost 3,450 francs last year, up from 2,790 francs in 2019, insurer AXA said, blaming costly high-tech parts.

stories.headline: Zurich's minimum wage of 23.90 francs an hour takes effect in January
more: About 70 percent of Zurich voters backed the wage in 2023. The city's chamber of commerce and an employers' group appealed, and in 2024 the Zurich administrative court ruled that the city's decision broke cantonal law.

The Federal Court overturned that ruling and upheld the rate. Employers have until December 31, 2027, to comply, and businesses in financial difficulty can ask the city council for a two-year transition.
stories.summary: The city of Zurich says its minimum wage of 23.90 francs an hour will take effect on January 1, 2027. Voters approved it in 2023, but business groups challenged it in court. The Federal Court ruled in May that Zurich and Winterthur had the power to set their own minimum wage.

stories.headline: EU rule change could add hundreds of millions to Swiss jobless costs
more: Swiss and EU officials discussed the revision at a joint committee on the free movement of people in Bern on Thursday. The EU told Switzerland its revised social security rules have taken effect in the bloc, and the Swiss side noted they bring major changes for unemployed cross-border workers.

Switzerland had 413,320 cross-border workers in the first quarter of 2026. The National Council is urging the Federal Council to reject the change, and the government says it will study the question in due course.
stories.summary: An EU reform would make the country where a cross-border commuter last worked pay that person's unemployment benefits, instead of the country where they live. Swiss officials estimate it could cost Switzerland 500 to 800 million francs a year. The Federal Council has not decided whether to adopt the change.

stories.headline: Landslide-hit village of Brienz to stay in red danger zone for at least a decade
more: A 2.3-kilometer drainage tunnel costing about 40 million francs was finished about a month ago. Boreholes now drain roughly 650 liters of water a minute, and the slope is moving less than 5 centimeters a year, ahead of the 10-centimeter target.
Drilling of more drainage boreholes is due to finish by summer 2027. A full long-term risk assessment is not expected for at least ten years.
stories.summary: Brienz in Graubunden will stay in the highest danger zone for at least another ten years, the canton's natural hazards commission found. The village has been in the red zone since 2017 because of a slow-moving landslide. Under cantonal rules, no new houses can be built there and existing ones may only be renovated.

briefs.text: A Microsoft cloud outage that began Thursday evening hit Outlook, Teams and other services in dozens of countries and disrupted Deutsche Bahn's email, making it harder to send out timetables for diverted trains. Microsoft said there were no signs of a cyberattack.

Only a third of Germans are satisfied with how democracy works in practice, and support for democracy as an ideal fell below 90 percent for the first time, a long-running University of Leipzig study found.

Germany fell to 25th place in the Climate Change Performance Index by Germanwatch and the NewClimate Institute, its third straight year of decline. The authors blamed the government's push to expand natural gas.
Siemens reported record profits, driven by demand from data centers. Chief executive Roland Busch said he expects the boom to continue despite the US midterm results.

stories.headline: Bundestag committee approves record 560.9 billion euro budget for 2027
more: The CDU/CSU-SPD coalition dropped planned cuts to housing benefit, kept a child supplement for low-income families but removed it for asylum seekers, scrapped a plastic packaging tax and a higher sparkling wine tax, and delayed a sugar tax on soft drinks to January 2028.

The coalition did not find the roughly 5 billion euros needed to cut electricity tax to the EU minimum, so that promised relief remains uncertain. Opposition lawmakers criticized the borrowing, while the government says it complies with the debt brake through exemptions for defense and infrastructure.
The defense ministry is set to receive 109.75 billion euros, plus nearly 30 billion euros from a special military fund, according to The Local.
stories.summary: The Bundestag's budget committee approved a record 560.9 billion euro federal budget for 2027 after a 16-hour session that ended at 6 a.m. Friday. The plan includes almost 123 billion euros in new borrowing, and more than 200 billion euros once debt-financed defense and infrastructure funds are counted. The full Bundestag is due to vote in its November 24-27 session.

stories.headline: Mercedes-Benz freezes new investment in German plants and weighs closures
more: HR chief Britta Seeger said Mercedes wants to avoid closures as far as possible. Production chief Michael Schiebe had earlier said one assembly plant and one powertrain plant could close if costs are not cut.

Mercedes says an hour of labor in German plants can cost up to five times as much as at its Eastern European sites. Chief executive Ola Kallenius defended the freeze and urged European policymakers to ease energy and regulatory burdens. The carmaker also faces weak demand in China, tariffs and cheaper Chinese electric cars.
stories.summary: Mercedes-Benz has halted all new investment at its German sites and says closing some factories is now a concrete option. Management blames high labor costs and says talks with employee representatives are deadlocked. The company wants longer working hours without higher pay, while the IG Metall union is seeking a 5 percent raise.

stories.headline: Study finds widespread sexual harassment in the German military
more: The plan includes an independent counseling center open around the clock, regular prevention training and specialist disciplinary lawyers. Critics want an outside body to investigate alleged cover-ups.

Applications for conscientious objection have nearly tripled since June, to 16,869 this year. Pistorius says troop numbers are at a 13-year high of about 190,000, while CSU leader Markus Soder is pressing for real conscription.
stories.summary: A study presented by Defense Minister Boris Pistorius found that 72 percent of female soldiers and 31 percent of male soldiers had faced verbal sexual harassment. More than 8,000 troops took part in the survey. Pistorius promised zero tolerance and a 34-point action plan.

briefs.text: China's carbon dioxide emissions fell 3.1% in the third quarter of 2026, the biggest quarterly drop since the 2022 Covid lockdowns, as coal power and transport oil use declined, according to an analysis for Carbon Brief.
The FDA granted tentative approval to Dr. Reddy's generic of twice-yearly HIV prevention shot lenacapavir, expected to cost about $40 per person per year in 120 low- and middle-income countries.
A family of six beavers was released near Loch Ness on Nov. 4, the first there in about 500 years; the Ness Beaver Project plans at least 15 family groups over three years.

stories.headline: Fewer people need treatment for neglected tropical diseases
more: The WHO published the figures on Nov. 4 in a mid-term evaluation of its road map for neglected tropical diseases, a group of infections that mainly affect the world's poorest communities. The report tracks progress toward the agency's 2030 targets.
stories.summary: The number of people requiring interventions against neglected tropical diseases fell to 1.41 billion in 2024, 36% fewer than in 2010, according to a new World Health Organization report. As of June 2026, 63 countries had eliminated at least one of these diseases.

briefs.text: Between 60 and 100 vehicles were stranded overnight on the E4 near Ornskoldsvik as a snowstorm hit northern Sweden. SMHI downgraded its red warning for the Skelleftea area to orange Friday morning.

A Gavle court found that a boy, now 14, fired the shots that wounded six people in central Gavle in October 2025 and convicted him of aggravated assault. He is too young for prison but must pay the victims 381,500 kronor.
Three Swedes were arrested in Spain on suspicion of sending fake invoices that brought in tens of millions of kronor, and Sweden will seek their extradition.
Stockholm police opened an attempted murder inquiry after a shot was fired at an apartment door in Gardet on Friday evening. No one was hurt and no arrests were reported.

stories.headline: Rival blocs hand Centre Party their offers as Sweden's deadlock drags on
more: Kristersson proposes a centre-right minority government of his Moderates, the Christian Democrats and the Liberals that would seek support in parliament issue by issue. To win the Centre Party over, he must convince it the Sweden Democrats would have no real influence.

Andersson's main problem is the Left Party, which still demands cabinet seats in a coalition the Centre Party refuses to join. Left leader Nooshi Dadgostar said Thursday it was up to the Centre Party to make a historic decision.
Kristersson is due to report to Speaker Andreas Norlen on Tuesday. If several prime ministerial votes fail, Sweden faces a new election within three months.
stories.summary: Social Democrat leader Magdalena Andersson and caretaker Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson each gave the Centre Party a full offer just after 5 p.m. Friday, meeting its deadline. The Centre Party holds the balance in the effort to form a government after September's close election. It plans to discuss the offers over the weekend and is not expected to respond until next week.

briefs.text: Microsoft said services were recovering after an outage that knocked out Outlook, Teams and Copilot worldwide from Thursday; it blamed a problem during a network capacity upgrade, not a cyberattack.
The FBI said it has seized more than $1.2 billion in cryptocurrency from the roughly $6.3 billion theft from Binance that it attributes to North Korean hackers.

SpaceX's Starship reached orbit on its 15th test flight, but the Super Heavy booster aborted its tower catch and fell into the Gulf of Mexico; SpaceX planned to try catching the ship itself on Saturday.
Rep. Lauren Boebert of Colorado lost her reelection bid to Democrat Eileen Laubacher, a retired Navy rear admiral, the AP projected; Democrats will hold at least 256 House seats in January.
Sen. Chris Van Hollen of Maryland is challenging Chuck Schumer for leader of the Senate Democrats in a December vote; Schumer says he has the votes.

stories.headline: Lutnick to testify as Bessent points to Commerce over chip sales to China
more: The firm, Megaspeed International, was previously led by Alice Huang, described by CBS News as a suspected Chinese spy who had an affair with Nvidia's Jensen Huang, who resigned as chief executive on Thursday. Some Republicans are asking why the company was never added to the U.S. Entity List.
Bessent declined to comment on reported tensions with Lutnick. Commerce did not immediately respond to CBS News. China, meanwhile, warned Washington against new export controls on computer chips.
stories.summary: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has agreed to testify before the Senate Banking Committee on Dec. 10, a U.S. official told CBS News, amid scrutiny of how his department policed exports of advanced AI chips. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Friday that Treasury, State, the Pentagon and the trade representative had favored blacklisting a Singapore firm suspected of routing Nvidia chips to China for months, but that Commerce controls the process.

stories.headline: Tanker strikes docked river cruise boat on the Mississippi
more: About 130 people were on board as the boat, operated by American Cruise Lines, finished an eight-day cruise through Louisiana and Mississippi; it had docked about two hours earlier. Several people were pulled from the water.
The tanker, the Marshall Islands-flagged Atlantic Asphalt, typically carries asphalt and bitumen. The river was closed to traffic, and the cause of the collision was not yet known.
stories.summary: A tanker hit the American Heritage, a five-deck paddlewheel cruise boat, on the Mississippi River in New Orleans on Friday at about 12:30 p.m., leaving it on its side in the water. The mayor said more than 30 people were being treated in hospitals and that all passengers were accounted for.

stories.headline: U.S. measles deaths reach 10 as elimination status hangs in the balance
more: Pennsylvania has reported seven deaths and 1,542 cases, Wisconsin two deaths and 651 cases, and New York one child's death. The CDC website lists six deaths; Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. reportedly asked the agency not to count deaths he said were not shown to be caused by measles.
The U.S., declared measles-free in 2000, could lose that status as soon as this week, which happens after 12 months of continuous transmission.
stories.summary: Wisconsin reported a measles-associated death of an infant on Friday, bringing the U.S. toll this year to 10 by state counts, Al Jazeera reported. The country has confirmed more than 5,400 cases this year, more than double the 2,289 recorded in 2025.

briefs.text: Car bombs killed a military officer in St. Petersburg and critically injured a former adviser to an ex-Ukrainian prime minister in Moscow; Russia blames Kyiv, which has not commented.
France called Israel's entry ban on far-left leader Jean-Luc Melenchon demagogic; Israel acted after France turned away a West Bank settler leader.
Nigeria completed 21 days of monitoring for 62 contacts of its first Ebola patient in over a decade, with no further infections.

stories.headline: EU names five countries for Ukraine talks as both sides launch mass drone strikes
more: U.S. envoy Jared Kushner said after meeting Vladimir Putin in Moscow on Thursday that Putin agreed to include Europe, but the Kremlin has not confirmed it. Europe has yet to agree on a single envoy; German Chancellor Friedrich Merz asked Washington for no surprises.

Russian officials said four people were killed in Volgograd, and Moscow's mayor reported drones over the capital. In Ukraine, Russian strikes damaged a Kyiv hospital, killed at least two people in Odesa and injured people in Zaporizhzhia, according to local officials.
stories.summary: EU leaders meeting in Dublin agreed that the bloc, along with Britain, France, Germany, Italy and Poland, will attend the next round of Ukraine peace talks, European Council President Antonio Costa said Friday. Overnight, Russia said it intercepted 1,198 Ukrainian drones over more than 15 regions, one of Kyiv's largest aerial attacks of the war.

stories.headline: UN watchdog presses Iran on hidden enrichment site; Turkey and Qatar sign defense pact
more: Also on Friday, Turkey and Qatar signed a mutual defense agreement in Istanbul after talks between President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani; its terms were not published. Turkey said it aims to prevent renewed war in the Gulf.

stories.summary: The International Atomic Energy Agency urged Iran in a report to member states to restore inspector access, calling the lack of information on an underground enrichment plant near Isfahan a proliferation concern. stories.headline: At least 10 killed in clashes over Guinea's gold mining ban
more: More than 1,200 people were arrested on suspicion of illegal mining this month, and the first mass trials opened this week. Mali says about 160,000 people have crossed into its territory from Guinea since the ban, and Burkina Faso says it has repatriated more than 45,000 citizens.
stories.summary: At least 10 people, including five foreigners, were killed and 13 injured when protesters clashed with security forces enforcing a ban on artisanal gold mining in Guinea's Siguiri region, the government said. The ban took effect on Nov. 2.
